---
title: >-
  OSDC - Open Source Diabetes Classifier
subtitle: "Diabetes type classification in Danish register data"
date: last-modified
---

OSDC is an open source algorithm that classifies everyone in Denmark as having
type 1 diabetes (T1D), type 2 diabetes (T2D) or no diabetes, based on data in
the national registers.

**Article:** [doi:10.2147/CLEP.S407019](https://doi.org/10.2147/CLEP.S407019)
**Documentation and code:**
[steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/)

## What does OSDC give you?

A pre-computed population with:

- **Diabetes type:** T1D, T2D or no diabetes
- **Onset date:** when the diabetes criteria were first met
- **Age at onset**

The classification is based on a combination of diagnosis codes (LPR),
medication information (LMDB) and laboratory results.

## When is it used?

- To **define a diabetes population** as an exposure or inclusion criterion
- To **exclude** diabetes patients from a control group
- To **classify type** - LPR alone is not sufficient to reliably distinguish T1D
  from T2D

## How to use OSDC

### DARTER - project 708421 (pre-computed file)

On DARTER the OSDC classification is already computed and ready to use (in
several formats). You do not need to run the algorithm yourself.

::: {.callout-important}
**New 2024 population - use this going forward** The osdc package has been
updated and cleared by CRAN, and a new diabetes population has been generated on
DARTER incorporating the latest data. It is valid for inclusions **until the end
of 2024** and is intended to be used **instead of** the previous population file
- not combined with it. The previous files remain unchanged for backward
compatibility and reproducibility.

The table is available in several formats:

- **Parquet:** `E:/workdata/708421/cleaned-data/parquet-external/osdc/2024` - on
  DARTER you can load it directly with `read_register("osdc")`
- **`.csv`, `.rds` or `.dta`:**
  `E:/workdata/708421/cleaned-data/diabetes_register_pop/2024`

::::: {.callout-warning}
The path and the filename `osdc` (and `read_register("osdc")`) are
**DARTER-specific** (project 708421). On other projects the file is named
differently and lives elsewhere.
:::::

The output format differs slightly from the old population. See the description
of the output variables - in particular the difference between **"raw"** and
**"stable"** inclusion dates (whether the inclusion date falls in a period with
sufficient inclusion-event data to be reliable) - in the [design
vignette](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/design.html#classify_diabetes).
:::

```r
# New 2024 population on DARTER - read_register resolves the path automatically:
library(fastreg)
dm_pop <- read_register("osdc")
```

<details>
<summary>Previous population (up to 2022) - for reproducibility only</summary>

The old file has a different output format than the 2024 population (the variable names below apply only to the old file).

```r
dm_pop <- readRDS("E:/workdata/708421/cleaned-data/diabetes-register-pop/dm_population_1977_2022.rds")

names(dm_pop)
# [1] "PNR"           "diabetes_type"  "do_dm"          "age_at_onset"

library(dplyr)
dm_pop <- dm_pop %>% rename(pnr = PNR)   # rename PNR to lowercase pnr

# diabetes_type: 1 = T1D, 2 = T2D  |  do_dm: onset date

# Example: filter to T1D patients
t1d <- dm_pop %>%
  filter(diabetes_type == 1) %>%
  select(pnr, diabetes_type, do_dm) %>%
  rename(date_diabetes = do_dm)
```

</details>

### Other projects - run the algorithm yourself

If your OSDC classification has not been pre-computed, you need to run the
algorithm yourself.

`osdc` is a **CRAN package** that can be installed on DST. It must be
**installed first** and then loaded:

```r
install.packages("osdc")
library("osdc")
```

On the DST server, `install.packages("osdc")` also updates the necessary
dependencies, which matters because the pre-installed packages may be outdated.

::: {.callout-note}
**Availability across projects** The package is confirmed available on
**DARTER** (project 708421). It is likely available on other projects too, but
this has not been verified - check yourself with
`"osdc" %in% rownames(available.packages())` on your own server (the package is
not pre-installed, so `available.packages()` shows whether it can be installed).
If a package is missing, you can **contact DST**, who can install requested
packages for you.
:::

See documentation and code on GitHub:
[steno-aarhus/osdc](https://github.com/steno-aarhus/osdc/tree/dd83510a6f1f62a12d0f978219dbfe9c9cc77f24)
and the getting-started guide at
[steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/osdc.html](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/osdc.html).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Data requirements: which registers and variables do you need?

`osdc` (version 0.11.3) requires **11 tables**. The package can **not** read
`.sas7bdat`: the data must be stored as parquet and opened as DuckDB objects.
Each register must be **one table with all years stacked** (not one file per
year).

See the [data sources
vignette](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/data-sources.html).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Complete script: prepare the data and run osdc yourself

Written against **osdc 0.11.3** (CRAN).

If you are on **DARTER**, a finished OSDC population already sits under
`cleaned-data` (see above). You only need this script if you want to **modify
the algorithm** or **avoid conditioning on the future** (step 4).

::::: {.callout-important}
**LPR3F or LPR3A? You probably only have one of them.**

From 2019 onward, LPR3 data comes in **two delivery formats with the same
content**, and which one you have depends on your project's data delivery:

- **LPR3A** (called **LPR-A**, the newer delivery): the files are named
  `lpr_a_kontakt` and `lpr_a_diagnose`. These are the ones DARTER has.
- **LPR3F** (the original researcher extract): the files are named `kontakter`
  and `diagnoser`.

They cover the **same period** (2019-), it is not a before and an after. Run
only `prepare_lpr3a()` or `prepare_lpr3f()` for the format you actually have.
:::::

**0. Packages**

```r
#-----------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#-----------------------------------------------------
# [CHECK ON DST] The callout above says the package is only confirmed available on
# DARTER. Run "osdc" %in% rownames(available.packages()) on the project you are
# actually working on and note the answer, so the caveat can be made concrete.
install.packages("osdc") # also updates the dependencies (duckplyr, dbplyr etc.)

library(osdc) # the algorithm itself
library(fastreg) # read_register(): opens parquet registers as DuckDB tables
library(dplyr) # the verbs work directly on the DuckDB tables (translated to SQL)
library(arrow) # write_parquet() at the end

# The whole pipeline is lazy: nothing is pulled into RAM until the final collect().

# DST's pre-installed packages are often too old for osdc (e.g. duckplyr 0.4 from
# 2024, where osdc requires >= 1.1). install.packages("osdc") forces the update
# through, and you will probably have to repeat it after the server's weekly reset.
```

**1. Open the registers as DuckDB tables**

```r
#-----------------------------------------------------
# 1.1 Open the registers that need no fixing
#-----------------------------------------------------
# osdc cannot read .sas7bdat. On DARTER the registers already sit as parquet.
# Otherwise they have to be converted first: see path setup and conversion at
# https://dp-next.github.io/fastreg/
#
# read_register() is arrow::open_dataset() + arrow::to_duckdb(). You get a DuckDB
# table back (class tbl_duckdb_connection - exactly the one osdc requires), and
# every call shares the SAME connection, so the registers can be joined together.
#
# NB: read_register() can ONLY see registers converted with fastreg, i.e. datasets
# laid out as <register>/year=YYYY/part-XXX.parquet. Both the year= subfolder and
# the part- filename count. If the register is laid out differently,
# read_register() cannot find it, and you use read_parquet_dataset() instead:
#   lmdb <- read_parquet_dataset("E:/workdata/<project no>/cleaned-data/parquet-external/lmdb")
# Note: read_parquet_dataset() does NOT use the options() path. You have to write
# the FULL path, including any subfolders below the directory you set.
# See "When read_register() cannot find the register" in Phase 4 - File formats.
lmdb <- read_register("lmdb") %>% rename_with(tolower)
lpr_adm <- read_register("lpr_adm") %>% rename_with(tolower)
lpr_diag <- read_register("lpr_diag") %>% rename_with(tolower)
sysi <- read_register("sysi") %>% rename_with(tolower)
sssy <- read_register("sssy") %>% rename_with(tolower)
lab_forsker <- read_register("lab_forsker") %>% rename_with(tolower)

class(lmdb) # must contain "tbl_duckdb_connection"

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 1.2 BEF: reduce to ONE row per person
#-----------------------------------------------------
# BEF holds one row per person PER YEAR, and read_register reads every year. osdc
# joins bef on pnr alone, so several rows per person multiply the drug purchases
# in that join. distinct() runs lazily in DuckDB and costs nothing.
# osdc requires the birth date to be called foed_dato: if it is called foed_dag in
# your data, rename it here.
bef <- read_register("bef") %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  distinct(pnr, koen, foed_dato)

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 1.3 LPR3: two fixes that MUST be made (LPR-A only)
#-----------------------------------------------------
# Both are documented in osdc's getting-started vignette:
#  A) LPR-A contains duplicates of contacts from 2017-2018 that are also in LPR2.
#     Without the filter, the same hospital contacts get counted twice.
#  B) kont_starttidspunkt is a datetime. osdc requires a plain Date, otherwise the
#     type check stops with an error.
lpr3a_kontakt <- read_register("lpr_a_kontakt") %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  filter(indberetningssystem == "LPR3") %>% # A: drop the duplicates
  mutate(kont_starttidspunkt = as.Date(kont_starttidspunkt)) # B: datetime -> Date

lpr3a_diagnose <- read_register("lpr_a_diagnose") %>%
  rename_with(tolower)

# If you have LPR3F instead, neither fix applies, but the identifier is usually
# called cpr and must be renamed to pnr:
# lpr3f_kontakter <- read_register("kontakter") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>% rename(pnr = cpr)
# lpr3f_diagnoser <- read_register("diagnoser") %>% rename_with(tolower)

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 1.4 Optional: cut the registers down to your own cohort
#-----------------------------------------------------
# The classification happens person by person, so this changes NOTHING in the
# result - it just makes everything much faster.
# The diagnosis tables (lpr_diag, lpr_a_diagnose) have no pnr and must not be
# filtered: they are inner-joined onto the contact tables inside prepare_*().
#
# Your cohort is stored as .rds, i.e. a plain data.frame in R. You can NOT join a
# data.frame directly onto a DuckDB table: it first has to be moved to the DuckDB
# side with to_duckdb(), which lands on the same shared connection that
# read_register() uses.
cohort <- readRDS("E:/workdata/<project no>/my_cohort.rds") %>% # pnr (+ index_date)
  to_duckdb()

bef <- bef %>% semi_join(cohort, by = "pnr")
lmdb <- lmdb %>% semi_join(cohort, by = "pnr")
lab_forsker <- lab_forsker %>% semi_join(cohort, by = "pnr")
lpr_adm <- lpr_adm %>% semi_join(cohort, by = "pnr")
lpr3a_kontakt <- lpr3a_kontakt %>% semi_join(cohort, by = "pnr")
sysi <- sysi %>% semi_join(cohort, by = "pnr")
sssy <- sssy %>% semi_join(cohort, by = "pnr")
```

**2. Check the data BEFORE running the algorithm**

Do **not** convert types at random. The osdc authors write that the types are
usually already correct after the SAS-to-parquet conversion: *"you should not
need to do any further type conversion"*. Check instead, and only fix what
fails.

The **names**, on the other hand, must match exactly: osdc picks the variables
with `all_of()`, so a variable called something else (e.g. `foed_dag` instead of
`foed_dato`) is an error. Upper and lower case does not matter, osdc handles
that itself.

```r
#-----------------------------------------------------
# 2.1 Types: the same check osdc performs internally
#-----------------------------------------------------
# [CHECK ON DST] This function is written, but has not been run. Verify three
# things before it can stand as a recipe:
#  1) str(registers()[["bef"]]$variables) - does it have the columns name and data_type?
#  2) do the data_type strings match R's class() 1:1 (character/Date/numeric/integer)?
#     If they do not, the ok column comes out FALSE for everything for no reason.
#  3) does head() %>% collect() work on all the registers, including the big ones?
check_types <- function(data, register) {
  expected <- registers()[[register]]$variables %>% select(name, data_type)

  actual <- data %>%
    head() %>%
    collect() %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), ~ class(.x)[1])) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      everything(),
      names_to = "name",
      values_to = "actual_type"
    )

  expected %>%
    left_join(actual, by = "name") %>%
    mutate(ok = data_type == actual_type) # FALSE = fix it in 2.2
}

check_types(bef, "bef")
check_types(lmdb, "lmdb")
check_types(lpr_adm, "lpr_adm")
check_types(lab_forsker, "lab_forsker") # and so on for every register you use

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 2.2 Fix ONLY what the check complains about
#-----------------------------------------------------
# The fixes are lazy mutate() calls on the DuckDB table and cost nothing:
#
#   koen is numeric     -> mutate(koen = as.integer(koen))       # 1 = man, 2 = woman
#   volume/apk integer  -> mutate(volume = as.numeric(volume), apk = as.numeric(apk))
#   pnr is a number     -> mutate(pnr = as.character(pnr))       # do it the SAME way everywhere
#   honuge is a number  -> mutate(honuge = as.character(honuge)) # osdc zero-pads to yyww itself
#   value is text       -> mutate(value = as.numeric(value))     # NB: "5,4" with a comma becomes NA
#   a date is datetime  -> mutate(samplingdate = as.Date(samplingdate))
#
# Example:
lmdb <- lmdb %>%
  mutate(
    volume = as.numeric(volume), # DDD in the package. MUST be numeric, not integer
    apk = as.numeric(apk) # number of packages. MUST be numeric, not integer
  )

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 2.3 Values: what does NOT fail, but gives you a wrong answer
#-----------------------------------------------------
# The LPR3 specialty is recognised from the TEXT, not from a code. If your values
# do not match the list in the algorithm, no LPR3 contact counts as either
# endocrinology or medical - and the T1D/T2D split falls apart without anything
# failing at all.
lpr3a_kontakt %>%
  count(kont_ans_hovedspec) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  collect() %>%
  print(n = 50)

# [CHECK ON DST] Verify the list path: run names(algorithm()) and see whether the
# elements really are called lpr3_is_endocrinology_dept / lpr3_is_medical_dept, and
# whether $logic is the field holding the value list. Otherwise fix the two lines below.
algorithm()$lpr3_is_endocrinology_dept$logic # the expected values (osdc lowercases them itself)
algorithm()$lpr3_is_medical_dept$logic

# Diagnosis types and retracted diagnoses: expected to be "A"/"B" and "Ja"/"Nej".
lpr_diag %>% count(c_diagtype) %>% collect()
lpr3a_diagnose %>% count(diag_type, senere_afkraeftet) %>% collect()

# c_spec must be readable as a number (8 = endocrinology, 1-30 = other medical).
lpr_adm %>% count(c_spec) %>% arrange(desc(n)) %>% collect() %>% head(20)

# Podiatrist services: must return more than 0 rows.
sssy %>% filter(substr(speciale, 1, 2) == "54") %>% count() %>% collect()
```

**3. Run the algorithm**

```r
#-----------------------------------------------------
# 3.1 Prepare and stack LPR
#-----------------------------------------------------
# LPR2 and LPR3 are prepared separately (diagnoses + contacts are joined and the
# codes are translated into logical flags) and then stacked into ONE lpr object.
# Use named arguments: the order in prepare_lpr2() is (lpr_adm, lpr_diag).
lpr <- list(
  prepare_lpr2(lpr_adm = lpr_adm, lpr_diag = lpr_diag),
  prepare_lpr3a(lpr3a_kontakt = lpr3a_kontakt, lpr3a_diagnose = lpr3a_diagnose)
  # If you have LPR3F instead:
  # prepare_lpr3f(lpr3f_kontakter = lpr3f_kontakter, lpr3f_diagnoser = lpr3f_diagnoser)
) %>%
  join_registers()

# The health insurance registers are stacked into one (sysi 1990-2005, sssy 2006-)
hsr <- list(sysi, sssy) %>% join_registers()

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 3.2 Classify
#-----------------------------------------------------
diabetes <- classify_diabetes(
  lpr = lpr,
  hsr = hsr,
  lab_forsker = lab_forsker,
  bef = bef,
  lmdb = lmdb,
  # The first date at which an inclusion can count as a TRUE incident case.
  # The default (1998-01-01) is one year after LPR's pregnancy data become valid
  # enough to exclude gestational diabetes. If your LPR/LMDB data only start in,
  # say, 2005, set it one year later ("2006-01-01").
  stable_inclusion_start_date = "1998-01-01"
) %>%
  collect() # only here is the result pulled into RAM

# Only people WITH diabetes are included (i.e. 2 or more inclusion events).
# stable_inclusion_date is NA if the inclusion falls before the date above: the
# person has diabetes, but the onset date cannot be used as incident.
diabetes %>% count(has_t1d, has_t2d, stable = !is.na(stable_inclusion_date))
```

**4. Variant: a classification that only sees data before your index date**

This is what solves the conditioning-on-the-future problem (see the warning
below). Filter **the raw date in each register** before you call `prepare_*()`
and `classify_diabetes()`.

The price is sensitivity: inclusion requires **two** events, so a person whose
second event only falls after the index date counts as "no diabetes" at
baseline. That is the right price to pay for not conditioning on the future, but
it has to be a deliberate choice.

```r
#-----------------------------------------------------
# 4.1 One shared index date for the whole cohort
#-----------------------------------------------------
index_date <- as.Date("2015-01-01")

lmdb_pre <- lmdb %>% filter(eksd < index_date)
lab_forsker_pre <- lab_forsker %>% filter(samplingdate < index_date)
lpr_adm_pre <- lpr_adm %>% filter(d_inddto < index_date)
lpr3a_kontakt_pre <- lpr3a_kontakt %>% filter(kont_starttidspunkt < index_date)
# For LPR3F: lpr3f_kontakter %>% filter(dato_start < index_date)

# The diagnosis tables are not filtered: they have no date, but they are
# inner-joined onto the contact tables, which now only reach the index date.

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 4.2 The health insurance registers only hold year + week (honuge)
#-----------------------------------------------------
index_year <- as.integer(format(index_date, "%Y"))
index_week <- as.integer(format(index_date, "%V")) # ISO week number

filter_before_index <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    mutate(
      yy = as.integer(substr(honuge, 1, 2)),
      ww = as.integer(substr(honuge, 3, 4)),
      # honuge is not Y2K safe: 90-99 is the 1990s, 00-89 is the 2000s.
      year = if_else(yy >= 90L, 1900L + yy, 2000L + yy)
    ) %>%
    filter(year < index_year | (year == index_year & ww < index_week)) %>%
    select(-yy, -ww, -year)
}

sysi_pre <- filter_before_index(sysi)
sssy_pre <- filter_before_index(sssy)

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 4.3 Does every person have their OWN index date?
#-----------------------------------------------------
# The cohort was already joined on in step 1.4. Here we use its index_date column
# instead of one shared date. Note: index_date is now the COLUMN from the cohort,
# not the R variable above - dbplyr always picks the column when the names collide.
lmdb_pre <- lmdb %>%
  inner_join(cohort, by = "pnr") %>%
  filter(eksd < index_date) %>%
  select(-index_date)

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 4.4 Run step 3 again - but with the _pre objects
#-----------------------------------------------------
# This is all of step 3 once more. Check every single argument: forget one _pre
# (typically sysi/sssy in hsr) and the algorithm still sees data after the index
# date, so the whole point of step 4 is gone without anything failing.
lpr_pre <- list(
  prepare_lpr2(lpr_adm = lpr_adm_pre, lpr_diag = lpr_diag),
  prepare_lpr3a(
    lpr3a_kontakt = lpr3a_kontakt_pre,
    lpr3a_diagnose = lpr3a_diagnose
  )
) %>%
  join_registers()

hsr_pre <- list(sysi_pre, sssy_pre) %>% join_registers()

# [CHECK ON DST] bef goes in unfiltered: it only holds foed_dato and koen, i.e. no
# date to cut on. But distinct() in step 1.2 pulls every year, so people who only
# immigrate AFTER the index date are included too. This should not change the
# classification (it requires events before index), but compare nrow(diabetes)
# with and without a bef cut to years <= the index year. If the numbers match,
# this comment can be deleted; if they differ, it belongs in the prose.
diabetes <- classify_diabetes(
  lpr = lpr_pre,
  hsr = hsr_pre,
  lab_forsker = lab_forsker_pre,
  bef = bef, # bef has no date to filter on
  lmdb = lmdb_pre,
  stable_inclusion_start_date = "1998-01-01"
) %>%
  collect()
```

**5. Save the result and link it to your cohort**

```r
#-----------------------------------------------------
# 5.1 What is in the output?
#-----------------------------------------------------
# classify_diabetes() gives you ONLY these five columns:
#   pnr, raw_inclusion_date, stable_inclusion_date, has_t1d, has_t2d
# [CHECK ON DST] Verify with names(diabetes). If there are more or different
# columns, both the list here and the select() below need fixing. Check the claim
# that has_t2d is exactly !has_t1d at the same time: table(diabetes$has_t1d,
# diabetes$has_t2d) should give zeros on the diagonal (nobody with both, nobody
# with neither).
# Neither the diabetes type as a single column nor the age at onset is in the
# output. You make both yourself (the old DARTER file had them, the new one does not).
diabetes <- diabetes %>%
  mutate(
    # Collapses the two logical columns into one label. has_t2d is by definition
    # !has_t1d, so everyone with diabetes gets either "T1D" or "T2D".
    diabetes_type = if_else(has_t1d, "T1D", "T2D")
  ) %>%
  # Keep both the type and BOTH dates.
  select(
    pnr,
    diabetes_type,
    has_t1d,
    has_t2d,
    raw_inclusion_date,
    stable_inclusion_date
  )

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 5.2 Save
#-----------------------------------------------------
# Save it in your own workdata folder, not in rawdata.
write_parquet(diabetes, "E:/workdata/<project no>/osdc_classification.parquet")

#-----------------------------------------------------
# 5.3 Link it to the cohort and compute age at onset
#-----------------------------------------------------
# Here we work in RAM: diabetes was collect()'ed in step 3.2. The cohort object
# from step 1.4, by contrast, sits on the DuckDB side and cannot be joined onto a
# data.frame directly. Read the cohort back in as a plain data.frame.
my_cohort <- readRDS("E:/workdata/<project no>/my_cohort.rds")

# The birth date comes from bef: it is not part of osdc's output.
birth_dates <- bef %>% select(pnr, foed_dato) %>% collect()

my_cohort <- my_cohort %>%
  left_join(diabetes, by = "pnr") %>%
  left_join(birth_dates, by = "pnr") %>%
  mutate(
    has_diabetes = !is.na(raw_inclusion_date), # no match = no diabetes
    age_at_onset = as.numeric(raw_inclusion_date - foed_dato) / 365.25
  )
```

::::: {.callout-warning}
**If you modify the algorithm, the published validation no longer applies.**
That also holds if you extend the events (e.g. GLP1-RAs) or change the
thresholds.
:::::
:::

## Coverage and limitations

- The DARTER dataset has a cohort built with osdc; the new 2024 population is
  valid for inclusions **until the end of 2024**
- Classifies **everyone** in Denmark - not just your cohort
- Uses LPR, LMDB and laboratory results - requires access to these registers

::: {.callout-note}
**Which diabetes drugs count as events?** Not all glucose-lowering drugs (ATC
`A10`) count as inclusion events in the algorithm:

- **ALL GLP1-RAs are excluded** as events, because this drug class is used
  extensively for weight loss among individuals without diabetes.
- For **SGLT2 inhibitors**, the pure **dapagliflozin and empagliflozin**
  preparations are also not included as events (recommended in Danish guidelines
  for heart and kidney failure among individuals without diabetes).
- **Combination preparations** of GLP1-RAs or SGLT2 inhibitors together with
  other glucose-lowering drugs, by contrast, **do** count as events.

See the exact logic in the algorithm vignette:
[steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/algorithm.html](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/algorithm.html)
- or the code directly on GitHub:
[steno-aarhus/osdc](https://github.com/steno-aarhus/osdc/tree/dd83510a6f1f62a12d0f978219dbfe9c9cc77f24).
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
**OSDC's type classification conditions on the future - be careful with the
pre-computed population** The pre-computed OSDC population can assign a person's
diabetes **type** based on events that occur **after** your index/inclusion
date. T1D vs. T2D is determined partly from insulin purchase patterns over time,
so the type can depend on information that did not yet exist on your index date.
If you use the type as a baseline variable, you are effectively **conditioning
on the future** (immortal time bias).

**Workaround:** run the algorithm **yourself** and filter the input registers to
only data **before your index date**, so `classify_diabetes()` only sees
pre-index information. Then the type classification is not contaminated by
future events. See step 8 of the script above ("Complete script: prepare the
data and run osdc yourself").

Note that if you modify the algorithm, e.g. if you want to include GLP1-RAs as
events, the **published validation no longer applies**.
:::

See the full methodology in the article and documentation site.

::: {.callout-tip}
**On DARTER you do not need to run any of this.** A finished OSDC extract
already sits under `cleaned-data` (the 2024 population, see the top of the
page). Only run the algorithm yourself if you want to **modify it** or **avoid
conditioning on the future** by feeding it only data from before your index
date.
:::
